name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Anthropic’s latest Claude 3.7 Sonnet as EXCAVA’s core reasoning engine. Its 200K-token context window and 64K-output tokens let us process longer documents and richer outputs without chunking, cutting latency by ~15% on complex queries. The trade-off is higher cost per token—about 3x Sonnet 3.5—but the jump in reasoning depth justifies it for high-value tasks where precision beats speed.

name: Torque
text: The real risk isn’t just the 3x cost spike—it’s the 2x margin erosion on every run when Sonnet 3.7 hits its 64K-output ceiling, forcing us to split outputs and reintroduce chunking latency we just cut. Instead, test Llama 4 Maverick at 128K context with 16K output tokens; it’s half Sonnet’s cost, scales better, and avoids the cliff-edge trade-off. Run a 50-query A/B against Sonnet 3.7 on EXCAVA’s top 10% hardest prompts—if Maverick cuts latency 10% with no margin loss, adopt it; else, revisit Sonnet with a 2x cost cap.
